reasoning_quality_informational.v1_root_problem: Billing dispute ticket volume doubled from ~600/month (Jun–Jul 2026) to ~1220/month (Aug–Sep 2026) (E-02), not because response handling is slow (E-01 shows median/p90 times within the 3.0-day SLA), but at least partly because field manual-read route completion fell to 0.88 against a 0.95 target across 9200 accounts in Aug–Sep (E-03), forcing estimate substitution that accounts for the 1240 ESTIMATED-read-type disputed bills (E-04). This mechanism does not explain the majority of disputes, which involve ACTUAL-read-type bills (1785/3025, E-04) whose cause is not yet established (tariff change ruled out, E-06).
reasoning_quality_informational.v2_root_problem: Billing dispute ticket volume doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to ~1220/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-02), not because response handling is slow (E-01: median 1.6d/p90 2.8d within 3.0d SLA) or a tariff change (E-06), but because billing-import rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 (E-13), compares raw AMI register values directly against 12-month m3-based consumption history with no unit scaling; firmware v4.2 meters (rolled out June 2026) report register values in 0.1 m3 units versus v3.x's plain m3 (E-14), so BV-17 misclassifies valid on-time v4.2 reads as high-consumption and rejects them at import (E-12: 1184/1240 ESTIMATED-type disputed bills had an on-time read rejected this way), forcing estimate substitution and wrong bills for those accounts. This explains the ESTIMATED-type share of disputes (1240/3025, E-04) but not the larger ACTUAL-type share (1785/3025, E-04), whose cause remains unestablished.
reasoning_quality_informational.ideal_final_problem: BV-17 validation rejects valid firmware-v4.2 AMI reads (unit-scale mismatch on H-MDMS-BILL) and substitutes estimates.
